chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to hold the dyer, the launderer, and the goldsmith liable, as a precaution for the belongings of the people. And he did not hold them liable for drowning, fire, or an overwhelming occurrence.

And when the ship sinks along with what is in it, and people recover it, then whatever the sea casts onto its shore belongs to its owners, and they have the greater right to it. And whatever people dive for, after its owner has abandoned it, then it belongs to them.

key_terms.السَّفِينَةُ: the ship whose cargo is discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الصَّائِغَ: the goldsmith entrusted with valuables for workmanship
key_terms.الصَّبَّاغَ: the dyer entrusted with people's goods for work
key_terms.الْغَرَقِ: loss caused by drowning or sinking
key_terms.الْقَصَّارَ: the launderer or cloth cleaner entrusted with garments
key_terms.غَاصَ: to dive and recover submerged property
key_terms.يُضَمِّنُ: to hold legally liable for loss or damage

ai.seo_question: When is a craftsman liable for entrusted property, and who owns goods recovered after a shipwreck in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings attributed to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding liability for entrusted goods and ownership of recovered property after a shipwreck. It distinguishes between ordinary professional liability taken as precaution for people's property and losses caused by overpowering events, while also clarifying the rights of original owners versus salvagers.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3927 - Commander of the Faithful (as) used to hold the dyer, launderer, and goldsmith liable as a precaution to protect people's belongings. However, he did not hold them liable for damages caused by drowning, fire, or overwhelming events.

And if a ship sinks along with its cargo, and people recover what washes up on the shore, it belongs to its owners, and they have the strongest claim to it. But whatever people dive for and the owner abandons, it belongs to those who recover it.
